response.title: Old City of Jerusalem in brief
response.summary: The Old City of Jerusalem is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
response.narrative:
The Old City of Jerusalem is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It sits at the heart of Jerusalem and covers roughly 0.9 square kilometres, yet it contains a very large number of religious and historical sites. It is surrounded by stone walls built in the 16th century CE under the Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, with eight main gates. The Old City is divided into four quarters - Muslim, Christian, Armenian and Jewish - and is a spiritual and cultural centre for millions of people worldwide.

A few facts:
- Area: approximately 0.9 km².
- Surrounded by Ottoman walls roughly 4 km long.
uncertainty_notes: Gaps the AI must not fill: exact founding date, population figures, and the precise dating of individual gates are not established in the source. If a request needs them, the AI must return an uncertainty note instead of guessing.
